Package io.webagent4j.extraction.api

Record Class ExtractionRequest<T>

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
io.webagent4j.extraction.api.ExtractionRequest<T>
Type Parameters:
T - the converted extraction result's type
public record ExtractionRequest<T>(LocatorDefinition source, ExtractionReadType readType, Optional<String> attributeName, IValueConverter<T> converter, Optional<IExtractionValidator<T>> validator) extends Record
Immutable, backend-neutral description of one extraction intent: where to find the source (source(), reusing the existing deterministic locator resolution - no second DOM resolution engine), what raw datum to read from it (readType()), and how to deterministically convert and validate that raw value.

The same request describes both a single extraction (one source, one result) and a list extraction (every matching source, one result per candidate, in the engine's deterministic order) - which of the two applies is a property of which extraction engine method a request is passed to, not of the request itself. source()'s own LocatorDefinition.timeout()/LocatorDefinition.stability() govern the wait, exactly as they already do for IFrame#locate: extraction introduces no separate timeout concept.

A converter is always present - text(io.webagent4j.locator.api.LocatorDefinition)/attribute(io.webagent4j.locator.api.LocatorDefinition, java.lang.String)/value(io.webagent4j.locator.api.LocatorDefinition) start with IValueConverter.identity() - so an extraction engine never has to fall back to an unchecked cast for a request with no converter attached. The pipeline is always raw -> convert -> validate: convert(IValueConverter) changes the request's result type and therefore always discards any previously attached validator (a validator typed for the old result type can never apply to the new one); attach validate(IExtractionValidator) again afterward.

    • convertAndValidate

      public T convertAndValidate(String raw)
      Applies this request's converter and, when present, its validator to an already-read raw value, in the mandated raw -> convert -> validate order. A converter that returns null is treated as a conversion failure - a successful ExtractionResult must never carry a null value - rather than letting a null silently reach a validator or a caller.
      Throws:
      ExtractionConversionException - if converter fails or returns null
      ExtractionValidationException - if the converted value fails validator()
